messages:
jamie: uploaded a quick perf snapshot from yesterday's canary. seeing weird tail spikes after we enabled the new classifier that buckets by prompt+decode-rate. P50 looks fine but P99 jumps.
perf-bot: perf/reports/1779989001/trace.html uploaded (profile + flamegraphs). :file_folder:
sasha: thanks — will grab the trace. do we still use the old kernel selector fallback for small prompts?
jamie: yes, selector still on. the strange bit: when classifier marks a request as 'short-highdecode' we force the low-latency kernel, but queueing sometimes bundles 4 of them and the kernel saturates GPU SMs -> stalls.
raju: that sounds like token-budget misclass. saw eviction churn in KV cache logs around the same times. keys evicted mid-request for a couple of sessions.
lee: can you paste the classifier thresholds? curious what counts as high decode.
jamie: current probe config (approx):
```
classifier:
  prompt_len_buckets: [0, 64, 256, 1024]
  decode_rate_buckets: [0, 20, 80, 9999] # tokens/sec
  mapping:
    - short-high: prompt<=64 && rate>=20
    - mid-low: 65-256 && rate<20
```
olivia: two quick thoughts: 1) threshold 20 t/s is pretty low for some models (opt-6/13) — they decode faster on FP16 kernels. 2) batching policy should respect effective-kernel-throughput rather than raw decode rate.
sasha: agree. maybe add an extra bucket for microbatches: short-ultrafast rate>=80 -> treat as single-request-per-batch to avoid SM contention.
raju: regarding KV evictions: our token-budget calc uses `max_budget = min(global_budget, per_request_budget)` but per_request_budget didn't account for queued decoded tokens from other requests in the same batch. result: eviction when combined decode exceeds `kv_capacity`.
jamie: repro steps I used:
- run 10k requests sampled from prod short prompts
- enable classifier mapping -> short-high
- set token_budget_target=64
- run with queue_policy=adaptive_token_budget
observed: P95 latency +120ms, P99 +420ms vs baseline
lee: try this config tweak for the queue policy (small test):
```
queue_policy: adaptive_token_budget
params:
  target_per_request: 48
  max_combined_tokens_per_batch: 256
  max_batch_delay_ms: 8
  prefer_single_request_for: short-ultrafast
```
olivia: also try swapping kernel choice: prefer "short-attn-fused" only when batch_size<=2, otherwise fall back to vectored kernel.
sasha: good idea. we should add an experiment matrix: vary target_per_request {32,48,64} x max_combined_tokens {128,256,512} x prefer_single_request boolean.
jamie: agreed. I'll run a canary tomorrow with that grid and attach traces. also will add extra logging for kv: `kv.eviction_trigger` and `batch.combined_token_count`.
perf-bot: scheduled job perf-grid-1779989001 at 2026-03-18T10:00Z :gear:
raju: FYI I saw one spike correlated with kernel selection path taking fallback that disabled async-copy; that adds ~30ms per call.
olivia: if you want I can PR a small selector rule: prefer fused kernel only when (batch_size <=2 && combined_tokens<=128 && avg_decode_rate>=20).
jamie: please do. once we have the grid results we'll pick the config that minimizes P99 without blowing up cost.
lee: can we also add a lightweight probe that emits `estimated_sm_util` per batch? would help correlate kernel choice -> SM saturation.
jamie: good call — adding that to the trace events.
sasha: thanks all, this is actionable. i'll follow up after the grid runs. :thumbsup:
